3. Abstract Dynamic Programs
This section is a brief review of the dynamic programming framework fromSargent and Stachurski(2025). We repeat the key definitions to make the paper partly self- contained.

3.1. **Definition and Properties.** An *abstract dynamic program* (ADP) is a pair (*V,* ❚), where
(i) *V* = (*V, ⪯*) is a poset and (ii) ❚ = *{Tσ*: *σ ∈* Σ*}* is a nonempty family of order preserving self-maps on *V*.
We call *V* the *value space*. Each operator *Tσ*in ❚ is called a *policy operator*. Σ is an arbitrary index set and elements of Σ are called *policies*. In applications, we impose conditions under which each *Tσ*has a unique fixed point. In these settings, the significance of each policy operator *Tσ*is that its fixed point, denoted below by *vσ*, represents the lifetime value of following policy *σ*.
